# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am establishing the communication code before any action: 👍 means YES, 👎 means NO, ✋ means HOLD, and 👌 means DONE. The bomb shows display 0, blue light, a large “PUSH TO DEFUSE” button, and three wires: blue, green, yellow. No one should act yet; Mute should consult the manual and report its verdict through the agreed code.

```text
speak(text="Communication code: thumbs up means YES; thumbs down means NO; open hand means HOLD; OK sign means DONE. Bomb view: display 0, blue light, large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Opening setup only: wait.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "✋", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👌]

Mute has sent three YES signals followed by DONE. I cannot safely infer a specific physical operation from that alone, so I am relaying the verdict in order rather than inventing an action. Blind should interpret it against the manual’s three required checks and act only if that yields an unambiguous instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Manual verdict received: YES, YES, YES, DONE. Apply these three YES results in the manual's required order; no additional action is specified by the signal.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Blind’s 🖐 signal is not part of the agreed code; HOLD was assigned to ✋. I therefore cannot treat it as an instruction or confirmation. I am asking Mute to relay that the signal is invalid and to provide Blind’s manual-derived action in words.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
speak(to="blind", text="Your raised-hand signal is not the agreed HOLD symbol. I cannot interpret it safely. Use your speech channel to state the required action; do not manipulate the bomb yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information reached me. The earlier three YES signals and DONE still do not identify which control to use, and 🖐 was not the agreed HOLD symbol. I am requesting the exact manual instruction from Blind in speech, while asking Mute to relay any resulting action using the agreed code or to wait if it is not unambiguous.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="State the manual's exact safe action in words now. Do not touch or manipulate anything until the action is unambiguous.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please relay Blind's exact requested action through the agreed signals; if it is not unambiguous, send HOLD.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute has signalled HOLD. Nothing should be touched or pressed yet. I am telling Blind to wait and asking Mute to provide the manual’s exact instruction using the agreed signals; the earlier YES sequence was not enough to identify a safe action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals HOLD. Do not touch, cut, or press anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please encode the manual's exact required action using the agreed signals. Use HOLD if the action is not yet unambiguous.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute has again signalled HOLD, so no physical action is authorized. To make the next report capable of identifying an operation, I am extending the gesture code: ✊ means press the button, and ☝, ✌, 🤟 mean cut wire 1, 2, or 3 respectively. Blind can hear this mapping and should tell Mute to use the appropriate action symbol, followed by DONE, only if the manual gives that definite instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute again signals HOLD; no action yet. Expanded report code: fist means press the button; index-up means cut wire 1; victory means cut wire 2; three-finger gesture means cut wire 3. Tell Mute to send the single manual-authorized action symbol followed by DONE, or HOLD if none is unambiguous.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute continues to signal HOLD, so no safe action has been identified. Blind must not press the button or cut a wire. I am asking Mute to distinguish “manual says HOLD” from “I need more information” using the agreed code, and asking Blind to wait for that verdict.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD persists. Do not press the button or cut any wire. Wait for an unambiguous manual verdict.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please distinguish whether the manual authorizes pressing, cutting wire 1, cutting wire 2, cutting wire 3, or only holding. Use the expanded action code followed by DONE; use HOLD only if no action is authorized.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute continues to send the agreed HOLD signal. I therefore treat the current safe state as “do nothing”: Blind must not press the button or cut any wire. The manual’s specific action still has not been communicated, so I am requesting a definitive action code rather than another provisional HOLD.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current verdict remains HOLD. Do not press the button or cut any wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please send the manual-authorized action, if any, using the expanded code: fist means press; index-up means cut wire 1; victory means cut wire 2; three-finger gesture means cut wire 3. Follow with OK for DONE. Otherwise continue HOLD.")
wait()
```
